question: Should OpenClaw accept `currentTokenCount` plus these SDK token-budget helpers as a stable public ContextEngine/plugin SDK contract now, or fold the token-budget signal into the broader assemble metadata RFC #82137?
rationale: The patch changes public plugin API and SDK exports that third-party context engines may compile against, while the broader assemble metadata design remains unsettled and related downstream use cases want more than token counts.

options.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Fixes
options.body: Approve `currentTokenCount` as a separate backward-compatible API after the count bug, generated baselines, docs map, and live proof are fixed.

options.title: Fold Into RFC #82137
options.body: Pause or close this PR and land token counts together with the broader provenance/internal-event assemble metadata design.

options.title: Keep Helpers Private For Now
options.body: Remove the SDK helper exports and defer public helper exposure until maintainers choose the permanent plugin API shape.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Fixes
recommendation.body: Approve `currentTokenCount` as a separate backward-compatible API after the count bug, generated baselines, docs map, and live proof are fixed.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to the PR and have the strongest recent merged history on the affected context-engine budget path.
